linkedin.hook: Formal verification of lending primitives is worthless if execution latency fails liquidations.
linkedin.copy:
Lending infrastructure on Soroban is shifting from pooled debt primitives toward isolated execution environments. Blend v2 formal pool verification solves smart contract invariant safety, but capital efficiency depends on execution pipelines. When margin routes through isolated SmartAccounts, collateral states maintain individual risk envelopes rather than sharing systemic pool drag.

The technical baseline reflects this separation. By decoupling margin custody from lending logic, Vanna routes directly into Blend b-tokens at 0.00014 XLM fixed gas overhead. The integration relies on ~320ms Mercury indexer latency to monitor positions against a strict 1.10x Health Factor floor. Liquidations and automated rebalances execute deterministically before price oracle drift impacts solvency.

Institutional liquidity cannot tolerate cross-collateral contagion or unverified pool states. Composable credit routing over formally verified b-tokens gives risk desks granular control over yield capture on Stellar. Builders and protocol risk teams can test contract interactions and deploy an isolated SmartAccount sandbox at test.stellar.vanna.finance.

Institutional architecture is documented at test.stellar.vanna.finance

reddit.hook: How we built isolated SmartAccount margin routing into Blend v2 b-tokens on Soroban testnet
reddit.copy:
We have been testing Blend v2 integration on Soroban testnet over the past few weeks, specifically around how composable credit can sit on top of b-tokens without introducing systemic collateral risk.

Most lending implementations on Stellar treat user accounts as direct pool participants. You supply assets, mint b-tokens, and your position lives inside the common pool state. The limitation here is capital lockup: if you want to run automated yield routing or leverage a position, you either sign every sub-call manually or delegate full custody to a monolithic contract.

We approached this by decoupling custody from execution using Soroban native SmartAccounts. Here is how the contract architecture operates on testnet:

1. Margin Custody and Delegation
A user spins up an isolated SmartAccount instance. The SmartAccount holds the primary balance and retains ownership of the minted Blend b-tokens. Instead of approving a central protocol to pull funds, the SmartAccount exposes scoped policy modules that only execute specific routing logic.

2. The Blend v2 Interface
When routing capital into Blend v2, the SmartAccount deposits underlying assets, receives b-tokens, and tracks debt shares against a hardcoded 1.10x Health Factor floor. Because Blend v2 uses formal pool verification for its math invariants, the SmartAccount treats the b-token pool as a deterministic interest-bearing sink.

3. Latency and Gas Constraints
State tracking runs through Mercury indexer webhooks with ~320ms latency. This allows the off-chain monitoring engine to detect undercollateralized positions and trigger rebalance calls before bad debt accrues. Execution cost comes out to roughly 0.00014 XLM fixed gas per invocation, making micro-rebalancing feasible even during high-frequency volatility.

If you are building yield strategies or liquidation bots on Soroban, you can test this flow yourself. We opened up the testnet deployment pipeline so you can deploy an isolated SmartAccount sandbox, supply mock collateral, and verify the b-token routing mechanics directly on chain.

Setup link: test.stellar.vanna.finance

Disclosure: I am a core engineer at Vanna Protocol working on our Soroban credit infrastructure.

The lighting adheres to the obsidian void aesthetic, and typography is correctly typeset with explicit Soroban testnet cues.

assets.mechanism_named: Automated SmartAccount yield routing versus manual un-leveraged spot supply

The visual contrast between the exhausted chemist manually handling glassware and the industrial robotic arm holding a sealed matte cell captures the thesis of manual Blend farming versus automated SmartAccount execution. However, the sealed container in the arm lacks visual indication that it is an isolated credit cell rather than generic lab hardware.
assets.fix: Ensure the robotic arm's payload more distinctly mirrors the architectural language of the isolated SmartAccount enclosure seen in primary assets.

assets.critique: Unacceptable on multiple fronts. Mechanistically, this is just a 4x4 neon grid with one tinted square, completely failing to depict isolated accounts or credit routing.
